title: Alternating tensor optimization and effective eigenproblems

items.title: Finite Hermitian ground vectors and a deterministic tie rule
items.statement: A finite real symmetric or complex Hermitian matrix attains its least Rayleigh quotient on a unit ground eigenvector; a standard-basis projection rule selects one deterministically from a degenerate ground eigenspace.

references.title: Ulrich Schollwöck, The density-matrix renormalization group in the age of matrix product states, Annals of Physics 326 (2011), §§6.3–6.4
Grégoire Misguich, Introduction to matrix-product states and tensor networks, complete lecture notes (2026), §2.7

items.title: Rayleigh energy perturbation for normalized finite states
items.statement: For unit vectors psi and phi in a finite tensor-array space and a Hermitian H, the energy difference is at most 2 times the operator norm of H times the distance between psi and phi.

references.title: Ulrich Schollwöck, The density-matrix renormalization group in the age of matrix product states, Annals of Physics 326 (2011), §6.3
Grégoire Misguich, Introduction to matrix-product states and tensor networks, complete lecture notes (2026), §2.7

items.title: Finite matrix-product states and Hermitian Hamiltonians
items.statement: Defines normalized finite real or complex MPS/TT states in open-boundary and periodic trace forms, finite Hermitian Hamiltonian inputs, and their Rayleigh energy.

references.title: Ulrich Schollwöck, The density-matrix renormalization group in the age of matrix product states, Annals of Physics 326 (2011), §§4.1–4.4
Grégoire Misguich, Introduction to matrix-product states and tensor networks, complete lecture notes (2026), §§2.1–2.4
Ivan V. Oseledets, Tensor-Train Decomposition, SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 33(5) (2011), §1

items.title: A periodic finite MPS has an exact open-boundary TT conversion
items.statement: A finite periodic trace MPS with cyclic bond dimensions r_k has an exactly equal open-boundary TT representation with internal bond dimensions r_0 r_k.

references.title: Ulrich Schollwöck, The density-matrix renormalization group in the age of matrix product states, Annals of Physics 326 (2011), §§4.1, 4.6
Grégoire Misguich, Introduction to matrix-product states and tensor networks, complete lecture notes (2026), §§2.1, 2.4.3

items.title: Rank-revealing QR sweeps give exact mixed canonical gauge
items.statement: Every nonzero finite open-boundary TT can be transformed without changing its tensor into a mixed canonical gauge; dependent bond directions are removed exactly by deterministic rank-revealing QR.

references.title: Ulrich Schollwöck, The density-matrix renormalization group in the age of matrix product states, Annals of Physics 326 (2011), §§4.1.2, 4.1.3, 4.4
Grégoire Misguich, Introduction to matrix-product states and tensor networks, complete lecture notes (2026), §§2.4.1–2.4.3

items.title: Canonical MPS environments are isometric and the effective Hamiltonian is Hermitian
items.statement: For a one-site or two-site center between left- and right-isometric TT environments, the center-to-full-state embedding is isometric and the pulled-back finite Hamiltonian is Hermitian.

references.title: Ulrich Schollwöck, The density-matrix renormalization group in the age of matrix product states, Annals of Physics 326 (2011), §§4.2, 4.4, 6.2–6.3
Grégoire Misguich, Introduction to matrix-product states and tensor networks, complete lecture notes (2026), §§2.4.3, 2.7

items.title: An exact local DMRG ground solve does not increase Rayleigh energy
items.statement: In a mixed canonical one-site or two-site subspace, replacing the current center by an exact lowest eigenvector of the effective Hermitian Hamiltonian weakly decreases the global Rayleigh energy before truncation.

references.title: Ulrich Schollwöck, The density-matrix renormalization group in the age of matrix product states, Annals of Physics 326 (2011), §§6.3–6.4
Grégoire Misguich, Introduction to matrix-product states and tensor networks, complete lecture notes (2026), §2.7

items.title: Finite alternating tensor optimization with effective eigenproblems
items.statement:
Work in exact arithmetic over a fixed field $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ and order $d\ge2$. The inputs are:

- a normalized finite MPS/TT state $\psi\in\mathbb F^{n_1\times\cdots\times n_d}$ together with one concrete presentation of $\psi$, either an open-boundary TT core list or periodic trace matrices; the supplied presentation must contract to $\psi$;
- a finite Hermitian Hamiltonian $H$ on that same tensor-array coefficient space;
- a positive integer sweep budget $M$;
- a window width $w\in\{1,2\}$; and
- optionally, positive integer rank caps $c_1,\ldots,c_{d-1}$.

The procedure is the following.

1. If the supplied presentation is in periodic trace form, convert it exactly to the open-boundary TT form using [[lem-na-periodic-mps-to-open-tt]]. Otherwise take the supplied open-boundary core list. Keep the resulting open-boundary core list.

2. For each of $M$ full sweeps, perform one forward pass and one backward pass. For width $w$, the windows are the $d$ single sites when $w=1$, or the $d-1$ adjacent site pairs when $w=2$. Visit them in increasing order in the forward pass and decreasing order in the backward pass.

3. Before each window update, place the TT in mixed canonical gauge about that window using the deterministic rank-revealing QR sweeps of [[lem-na-mixed-canonical-qr-gauge-preserves-state]]. Contract the fixed left and right cores to form the isometric center embedding $E$ and compute the finite effective matrix $H_{\mathrm{eff}}=E^*HE$.

4. Apply the exact ground-vector rule of [[lem-na-finite-hermitian-ground-vector-with-deterministic-tie]] to $H_{\mathrm{eff}}$. Let $x$ be the resulting unit eigenvector and replace the center coefficient vector by $x$. Record its local Rayleigh energy $x^*H_{\mathrm{eff}}x=\lambda_{\min}$ and residual $\|H_{\mathrm{eff}}x-\lambda_{\min}x\|_2$.

5. For a two-site window, reshape the updated center as a matrix with row index (left bond, first physical index) and column index (second physical index, right bond). Compute an exact compact SVD $X=U\Sigma V^*$. In a forward pass replace the first core by the reshape of $U$ and absorb $\Sigma V^*$ into the second core. In a backward pass absorb $U\Sigma$ into the first core and replace the second core by the reshape of $V^*$. Retain every positive singular direction, so this split changes no tensor entries. For a one-site window, keep that site as the center.

6. After each complete forward/backward sweep, if rank caps were supplied, apply [[alg-tensor-train-rounding]] to the current TT and record its cut tails $\delta_1,\ldots,\delta_{d-1}$ and $\tau=(\sum_{k=1}^{d-1}\delta_k^2)^{1/2}$. If $\tau<1$, normalize the rounded tensor and continue from it. If $\tau\ge1$, discard that rounded candidate, retain the last normalized unrounded tensor, and record status **rounding-skipped**. If no rank caps were supplied, do not round.

Return the final normalized TT state, the energy and local-residual records, all accepted discarded-tail records, and status **budget-complete** or **rounding-skipped** according to whether any requested rounding was skipped.

references.title: Ulrich Schollwöck, The density-matrix renormalization group in the age of matrix product states, Annals of Physics 326 (2011), §§6.2–6.4
Grégoire Misguich, Introduction to matrix-product states and tensor networks, complete lecture notes (2026), §2.7
Ivan V. Oseledets, Tensor-Train Decomposition, SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 33(5) (2011), §3
Mi-Song Dupuy, Tensor trains for high-dimensional problems, lecture notes (March 11, 2026), §§1.2.2, 1.2.4–1.2.5

items.title: TT discarded weights bound the post-sweep DMRG energy increase
items.statement:
Let $\psi_0$ be a normalized finite MPS/TT state with a supplied concrete open-boundary TT core list or periodic trace presentation contracting to $\psi_0$, and let $H$ be a finite Hermitian Hamiltonian on the same coefficient space. Run [[alg-na-alternating-tensor-optimization-and-effective-eigenproblems]] for one full forward/backward sweep of a fixed width $w\in\{1,2\}$, with $M=1$ and no rank caps, from that presentation using exact local solves and exact SVD splits; call its normalized unrounded output $\psi_*$. Apply exact TT rounding with rank caps $c_1,\ldots,c_{d-1}\in\mathbb N_0$, obtaining $\widetilde\psi$ and discarded tails $\delta_1,\ldots,\delta_{d-1}$. Put $\tau=(\sum_{k=1}^{d-1}\delta_k^2)^{1/2}$. If $\tau<1$, define $\phi=\widetilde\psi/\|\widetilde\psi\|_F$. Then
$$\mathcal E_H(\phi)\le \mathcal E_H(\psi_0)+4\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\tau.$$
In particular,
$$\mathcal E_H(\phi)-\mathcal E_H(\psi_*)\le4\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\tau.$$
No normalized-output claim is made when $\tau\ge1$.

references.title: Ulrich Schollwöck, The density-matrix renormalization group in the age of matrix product states, Annals of Physics 326 (2011), §§4.5, 6.4
Ivan V. Oseledets, Tensor-Train Decomposition, SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 33(5) (2011), §§2–3
Mi-Song Dupuy, Tensor trains for high-dimensional problems, lecture notes (March 11, 2026), §§1.2.2, 1.2.4–1.2.5

items.title: Convergent fixed-rank exact sweeps are coordinatewise stationary
items.statement: Fix a finite Hermitian Hamiltonian $H$ on the coefficient space of the states. Consider an infinite sequence obtained by repeatedly applying one full no-truncation sweep of [[alg-na-alternating-tensor-optimization-and-effective-eigenproblems]], starting from a supplied concrete open-boundary TT core list or periodic trace presentation representing a normalized state, with fixed bond dimensions and a fixed finite list of one-site or two-site update windows. Assume the canonical core arrays at every stage of each sweep are bounded and converge componentwise in one consistent gauge to a single normalized canonical core tuple. Then the limit is **coordinatewise stationary**, meaning that for each update window, its limiting center vector minimizes the Rayleigh quotient of the effective Hermitian Hamiltonian over all unit center vectors with the other limiting cores fixed. In particular, each limiting center is a lowest eigenvector of its limiting effective Hamiltonian. This is conditional on the stated convergence; it asserts neither convergence of DMRG nor global minimality.

references.title: Ulrich Schollwöck, The density-matrix renormalization group in the age of matrix product states, Annals of Physics 326 (2011), §§6.3–6.4
Grégoire Misguich, Introduction to matrix-product states and tensor networks, complete lecture notes (2026), §2.7

title: Alternating tensor optimization and effective eigenproblems — Examples

items.title: A two-site spin-chain local solve reaches the exact ground state
items.statement: For H=-Z tensor I-I tensor Z-Z tensor Z, the exact two-site update from |11> returns |00> and decreases energy from 1 to -3.

items.title: A degenerate local ground eigenspace has a deterministic tie choice
items.statement: For H=Z tensor Z, the degenerate two-site ground space is span{|01>,|10>}; the deterministic standard-basis rule returns |01>.

items.title: A two-site TT truncation can increase energy after an exact solve
items.statement: An exact local ground solve returns an entangled two-site ground state whose rank-one TT truncation is normalized to a higher-energy product state; the discarded-weight bound remains valid.
